svg.text: Exploratory K=11 LDA topics; 24 author-reviewed topic-threat associations (T03 has none).
Associations are not estimates of crime incidence, causation or preventive effectiveness.

path.title: topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Perceived personal-information privacy risks associated with adoption of metaverse business/finance services. Limits: Perception/adoption evidence does not establish actual privacy breaches. The human-identity-threat construct on p.8 concerns AI/workplace existential issues, not identity theft.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Modify: Modify: retain as “smart-contract vulnerability and project-anomaly detection”. Limits: A proposed/evaluated technical method; does not establish prevention in live use or cover all cyberattack types.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Promote: Avatar-cloning/impersonation risks addressed by a proposed detection/privacy-awareness framework. Limits: Described scenarios and a test-bed do not establish real-world victimisation or preventive effectiveness.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Modify: Modify: retain as “ML-based detection/classification of suspected fraudulent or malicious Ethereum/Bitcoin transactions”. Correct the seven-algorithm-ensemble description. Limits: Classification results and stated aims do not demonstrate a reduction in actual fraud or operational deployment.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Promote: Personal-information and behavioural-data privacy exposure addressed by the proposed NFT-avatar framework; replace the generic “data” keyword rationale. Limits: Do not claim measured breaches or field-proven prevention.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Promote: Attacks on avatar/virtual-entity trust and reputation systems, including Sybil, on/off and reputation manipulation. Limits: Included under the agreed scope covering associated platform-security risks. A direct financial-offence mechanism is not established.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Modify: Modify: retain as “audit/compliance governance and jurisdictional accountability challenges”; add the jurisdiction chapter when discussing actual gaps. Limits: Recommendations do not establish control effectiveness. The chapter supplies the authors' legal analysis, not an independent verification of current law.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Promote: Observed data-collection/disclosure inconsistencies and associated privacy exposure in the applications studied by METAseen. Limits: Do not generalise to all metaverse applications or imply proven legal violations or crime incidence.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept on Author C’s supplied passage: retain as a general fraud concern motivating audit controls. The independent source-check limitation remains recorded. Limits: A general fraud concern; no specific scam mechanism, incident rate or laundering pathway is established.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept with the stated perception caveat: “interviewed artists' perceived scam and suspicious-activity risks in NFT markets”. Limits: Interviews do not independently establish that alleged crimes occurred or measure their incidence. Keep the perception qualification visible.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: “identity/impersonation risks motivating avatar authentication”. Limits: A motivating risk, not an incident-frequency estimate. Supports the authentication strand more directly than the transaction-protocol strand.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: describe literature-discussed DeFi-related laundering/concealment mechanisms. Limits: Keep the p.11 finding that NFTs did not prompt an en masse switch away from established methods. That NFT-specific finding does not establish that all DeFi laundering is rare. No adoption-frequency estimate follows from the edge.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept with a narrow regulatory explanation: “supervisory and cross-jurisdiction governance challenges concerning DeFi/DEX activity”. Limits: A descriptive analysis of regulation and supervisory challenges; does not demonstrate effectiveness of particular measures.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: retain as literature discussion of cryptoasset fraud/scams. The Manning anchor supplies independently checked support even while Shim's PDF is unlocated. Limits: Review/case-synthesis material; not new measurement by this project. Maintain attribution to the cited literature.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Promote: Cross-chain/asset-hopping laundering exposure using bridges and decentralised exchanges; replace the Shim wallet-credential-theft rationale with Manning p.8, §9.1. Limits: Source support overlaps the DeFi edge and is not an additional independent incident finding. Credential theft alone does not establish laundering.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: “NFT-market manipulation risks discussed in the source”. Limits: Monetary and incident claims are attributed to other references. The relationship can be accepted without repeating the unverified monetary figure.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Promote: Potential quantum attacks on encryption/access-control security and the proposed post-quantum response. Limits: Retain the potential/future-risk framing; do not imply observed operational quantum attacks, measured crime incidence or field-proven protection.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: “privacy/data-protection concerns motivating encryption and access control”. Limits: A technical research motivation and proposed scheme; not measurement of actual breaches or proof of operational prevention.
topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: general platform-security threat discussion. Limits: A threat-landscape overview, not an incident-prevalence study.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Modify: Modify: retain specifically as “exploitation of smart-contract vulnerabilities”. Limits: Do not extend the entry to all DeFi/DAO/governance misuse. It is a threat-table entry, not a detailed case study.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: general legal/compliance and cross-border governance challenges. Limits: Does not establish a particular accountability-gap incident or evaluate a governance intervention.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: identity theft, impersonation and identity-related access risks. Limits: Multiple supporting discussions do not establish incident frequency or independent empirical confirmation of particular cases.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: privacy/data-protection concerns and their regulatory context. Limits: Regulatory discussion is not evidence of a documented breach.

topic-associated-with-threat [author_reviewed_k11_20261001] Accept: Accept: phishing/social-engineering pathways involving metaverse impersonation. Limits: A described threat pathway, not measured frequency.

g.title: T01: Perceived trust, equality and consumer issues 2.97% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 2 of 65 publications.
T02: Data-driven attack detection and authentication 14.39% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 11 of 65 publications.

T03: Gameplay and review/research methods 6.17% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 2 of 65 publications. No author-approved topic-threat link (insufficient reviewed support).
T04: Technical trust, reputation and authenticity 3.25% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 2 of 65 publications.
T05: Governance of data and assets 7.57% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 4 of 65 publications.
T06: NFT ownership and digital-asset markets 8.86% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 4 of 65 publications.
T07: Transaction and authentication protocols 9.65% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 6 of 65 publications.
T08: Cryptoasset crime and scams 8.57% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 6 of 65 publications.
T09: NFT markets, value and financial perceptions 3.20% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 2 of 65 publications.
T10: Encryption, access control and network methods 7.19% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 5 of 65 publications.
T11: Broad metaverse-platform security 28.18% mean publication-level topic proportion (thematic attention, not crime incidence); dominant topic in 21 of 65 publications.
